notes.text: **Shabbat 117b** — כַּמָּה סְעוּדוֹת חַיָּיב אָדָם לֶאֱכוֹל בַּשַּׁבָּת — שָׁלֹשׁ... וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ: ״וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אִכְלוּהוּ הַיּוֹם כִּי שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם לַה׳ הַיּוֹם לֹא תִמְצָאֻהוּ בַּשָּׂדֶה״... וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: בַּהֲדֵי דְּאוּרְתָּא. How many meals must one eat on Shabbat? Three; both views derive their count from the one verse, and the Sages count the three mentions of "today" including the evening. Rav Tzadok builds on the fact that only the first "today", the one matched to Friday night, carries the word "eat". *Mafteach: found*

**Exodus 16:25** — וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אִכְלֻהוּ הַיּוֹם כִּי שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם לַה׳ הַיּוֹם לֹא תִמְצָאֻהוּ בַּשָּׂדֶה. Moshe said: eat it today, for today is a Sabbath to Hashem; today you will not find it in the field. Only the first clause speaks of eating; the second and third "today" do not. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Exodus 16:23; correct: Exodus 16:25)*

**Zohar II 88a** (Yitro) — וְעַל כַּךְ, בָּעֵי לְסַדְּרָא פָּתוֹרֵיהּ בְּלֵילְיָא דְּשַׁבְּתָא, בְּנַהֲמֵי וּבִמְזוֹנֵי. רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר, אֲפִילוּ בְּיוֹמָא דְּשַׁבְּתָא נָמֵי. Therefore one must set his table on Shabbat night with bread and food; R. Yitzchak said: on Shabbat day as well. The "even" of R. Yitzchak implies that the night meal is the primary one, which is the inference Rav Tzadok supports from the verse. *Mafteach: found*

**Pesachim 105a** — כְּבוֹד יוֹם וּכְבוֹד לַיְלָה כְּבוֹד יוֹם קוֹדֵם. וְאִם אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא כּוֹס אֶחָד — אוֹמֵר עָלָיו... Honour of the day and honour of the night: honour of the day comes first; and if he has only one cup, he says over it... Because the baraita goes straight on to the single cup, Rav Tzadok limits its precedence to the wine of the day kiddush. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Achrei Mot 11** (Rav Tzadok) — sets the same Pesachim 105a against the same Zohar II 88a, noting that the Magen Avraham (271:4) already raised the contradiction; there he reconciles them differently: at night the holiness enters through what Israel brings into the meal, by day it comes from Hashem's side (the meal of Atika), so a choice delicacy is saved for the day. *checked*

**Pri Etz Chaim, Sha'ar HaShabbat 17** (R. Chaim Vital, from the Arizal) — on the Friday-night meal: דָּא סְעוּדָתָא דַּחֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין ... וּסְעוּדָה זוֹ דְּיִצְחָק שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל הַסְּעוּדָה ... וְכָל הַמְעַנֵּג סְעוּדָה זוֹ נִיצּוֹל מֵחֶבְלֵי מָשִׁיחַ; the morning meal is “נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם”. The night meal belongs to Yitzchak, its master. The link of the meals with the Avos is already in the Zohar (II 88b): סְעוּדָתֵי דְּאַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב כְּלִילָן בְּהוּ. *Mafteach: missing (now added)*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Vayera 6** (Rav Tzadok) — derives the three meals from the three "today" of Shabbat 117b and states the same order: the Friday-night meal is counted against Yitzchak and the day meal against Avraham, because from Israel's side one first turns from evil (the Zohar II 88b order of the verses) and only then rises; it adds a reading of the three meals as delight, rest and holiness. *checked*

**Genesis 27:4** — וַעֲשֵׂה־לִי מַטְעַמִּים כַּאֲשֶׁר אָהַבְתִּי וְהָבִיאָה לִּי וְאֹכֵלָה בַּעֲבוּר תְּבָרֶכְךָ נַפְשִׁי בְּטֶרֶם אָמוּת. Make me tasty food such as I love and bring it to me to eat, so that my soul may bless you before I die. This is the verse the whole os explains: why Yitzchak, alone of the Avos, asks for a meal, and why "such as I love". *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 21:8** — וַיִּגְדַּל הַיֶּלֶד וַיִּגָּמַל וַיַּעַשׂ אַבְרָהָם מִשְׁתֶּה גָדוֹל בְּיוֹם הִגָּמֵל אֶת־יִצְחָק. The child grew and was weaned, and Avraham made a great feast on the day Yitzchak was weaned. *Mafteach: found*

**Tosafot, Shabbat 130a**, s.v. *Shash anochi* — וכן אמרי' (פר"א פ' כ"ט) ויעש אברהם משתה גדול ביום הגמל את יצחק ביום ה"ג מל את יצחק דהיינו ביום השמיני דמילה כמנין ה"ג. Tosafot cite Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer: the feast was "on the day *he-gimel*", the day he circumcised (*mal*) Yitzchak at eight (ה״ג = 8), so it was the meal of a circumcision. The printed Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 29 gives the same law without the wordplay: חַיָּב אָדָם לַעֲשׂוֹת שִׂמְחָה וּמִשְׁתֶּה בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שֶׁזָּכָה לָמוּל אֶת בְּנוֹ (one must make a celebration on the day he merits to circumcise his son). *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Shabbat 129a; correct: Shabbat 130a)*

**Yoma 28b** (unnamed) — אָמַר רַב: קִיֵּים אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַע אַבְרָהָם בְּקוֹלִי״. Rav: Avraham kept the entire Torah, as it says "because Avraham listened to My voice". Hence a Shabbat or festival meal would already have counted as a mitzvah meal for the Avos. *Mafteach: missing*

**Shabbat 151b** — אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁמַּנִּיחִין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְעוֹשִׂין כׇּל יְמֵיהֶם כְּחַגִּים. These are people who abandon Torah and make all their days like festivals (expounding "the dung of your festivals", Malachi 2:3). So feasting on an ordinary weekday is censured, which sharpens the question about Yitzchak's request. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Shem MiShmuel, Toldot 6:12** (Chassidus) — asks the same question of the wording, why Yitzchak says "such as I love" and Rivkah repeats "such as he loves", and answers through the raising of fallen sparks: hunted food stands for forces brought under holiness against their will, fitting Yitzchak's attribute of *gevurah*.
ועשה לי מטעמים כאשר אהבתי, יש לדקדק שבסיפור רבקה ליעקב כתיב ועשה לי מטעמים ואוכלה ולא נאמר כאשר אהבתי

**Bereshit Rabbah 11:4** — רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּשֵׁם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אָמַר, מִפְּנֵי אִיסְטְנִיסִים בֵּרְכוֹ בְּמַטְעַמִּים. רַבֵּנוּ עָשָׂה סְעוּדָה לְאַנְטוֹנִינוּס בְּשַׁבָּת, הֵבִיא לְפָנָיו תַּבְשִׁילִין שֶׁל צוֹנֵן אָכַל מֵהֶם וְעָרַב לוֹ... אָמַר לוֹ שַׁבָּת הֵן חֲסֵרִין. Hashem blessed Shabbat with flavour: Rebbi served Antoninus cold dishes on Shabbat and he relished them; hot dishes on a weekday pleased him less, and Rebbi told him the missing spice was Shabbat. Rav Tzadok reads the "flavour" as the holiness the soul tastes in the food (1.20–21). The index cites 11:2, which is a different exposition (בֵּרְכוֹ בַּמָּן). *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Bereshit Rabbah 11:2; correct: Bereshit Rabbah 11:4)*
**Genesis 2:3** — וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת־יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ. God blessed the seventh day and made it holy; the midrash asks what the blessing consisted of. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Shem MiShmuel, Lech Lecha 11:29** (Chassidus) — reads the same Antoninus story: the serpent's poison spoils the taste of food, but on Shabbat the outside forces have less hold, a light of the future shines and the taste itself changes; Rav Tzadok makes the same contrast with Adam's mixed good and evil (5.20–21).
והיינו כי הארס של נחש פוגם טעם המאכל, אך בשבת שאין הטבע כ"כ מגושם ואין לכחות החיצונים שליטה כ"כ

**Berakhot 49a** (unnamed) — מְקַדֵּשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַזְּמַנִּים — יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּקַדְּשִׁינְהוּ לִזְמַנִּים. "Who sanctifies Israel and the seasons": it is Israel who sanctify the seasons. Hence a festival's holiness is what Israel bring into it, including its meals. *Mafteach: missing*

**Kiddushin 31a** and **Rashi** there — אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מֵרֵישׁ הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: מַאן דַּהֲוָה אָמַר לִי הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דְּאָמַר: סוֹמֵא פָּטוּר מִן הַמִּצְוֹת – עָבֵידְנָא יוֹמָא טָבָא לְרַבָּנַן; Rashi: יומא טבא לרבנן - סעודה לתלמידים. Rav Yosef, who was blind, said he would make "a good day" for the scholars for whoever settled his question; Rashi explains: a meal for the students. *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 1:4** (unnamed) — וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת־הָאוֹר כִּי־טוֹב. God saw the light, that it was good. Rav Tzadok reads *yoma tava*, "a good day", as the first light called "good" appearing in the meal. *Mafteach: missing*

**Shabbat 119a**, as applied by the **Yam Shel Shlomo, Bava Kamma ch. 7** — אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: תֵּיתֵי לִי, דְּכִי חֲזֵינָא צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּשַׁלִּים מַסַּכְתֵּיהּ, עָבֵידְנָא יוֹמָא טָבָא לְרַבָּנַן. Abaye: when I saw a young scholar complete his tractate, I made a festive day for the Sages. The Yam Shel Shlomo learns from this that the meal at a *siyum* is a *seudas mitzvah*. (The Yam Shel Shlomo is not available in the texts checked; Rav Tzadok gives the same reference, "עי' יש"ש ב"ק", in Peri Tzadik, Motzei Yom Kippur 3.) *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Motzei Yom Kippur 3** (Rav Tzadok) — the same two passages (Rav Yosef in Kiddushin 31a with Rashi's "סעודה לתלמידים", and Abaye at a *siyum*, Shabbat 119a, with the Yam Shel Shlomo) and the same question, "ומה זה לשון יומא טבא"; there he answers with *simchah*, that completing a mitzvah lets one bring festival joy into others' hearts, where here he answers with the light "כי טוב" entering the meal. *checked*

**Genesis 25:28** with **Targum Onkelos** — וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת־עֵשָׂו כִּי־צַיִד בְּפִיו; Onkelos: וּרְחֵם יִצְחָק יָת עֵשָׂו אֲרֵי מִצֵּידֵיהּ הֲוָה אָכִיל. Yitzchak loved Esav because game was in his mouth; Onkelos: because he used to eat of his catch. *Mafteach: found*

**Ramban, Genesis 25:34** — וְרַבִּי אַבְרָהָם מִשְׁתַּבֵּשׁ בְּכָאן מְאֹד, שֶׁאָמַר כִּי בִּזָּה הַבְּכוֹרָה בַּעֲבוּר שֶׁרָאָה שֶׁאֵין מָמוֹן לְאָבִיו... וְהָעֵד שֶׁהָיָה יִצְחָק אוֹהֵב אֶת עֵשָׂו בַּעֲבוּר צֵידוֹ... וְהַצַּיִד אֲשֶׁר הָיָה בְּפִיו, כֵּן יַעֲשׂוּ הַשָּׂרִים וְהַמְּלָכִים, בּוֹחֲרִים בַּצַּיִד מִכָּל מַאֲכָל. Ramban rejects Ibn Ezra's view that Yitzchak had become poor and so loved Esav for his game; game is simply the food that princes and kings prefer. *Mafteach: found*

**II Kings 3:15**, cited by **Ramban, Genesis 25:34** — וְעַתָּה קְחוּ־לִי מְנַגֵּן וְהָיָה כְּנַגֵּן הַמְנַגֵּן וַתְּהִי עָלָיו יַד־יְהֹוָה; Ramban: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ בְּנַפְשׁוֹ כִּי אַחַר הָאֲכִילָה הָיְתָה מִתְעַנֶּגֶת וּשְׂמֵחָה וְיָחוּל עָלֶיהָ רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ. Elisha: bring me a musician; as he played, the hand of Hashem came upon him. Ramban: Yitzchak knew that after eating his soul would be delighted and glad, and the holy spirit would rest on it. *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 27:9** with **Rashi** — וְאֶעֱשֶׂה אֹתָם מַטְעַמִּים לְאָבִיךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר אָהֵב; Rashi: כאשר אהב. כִּי טַעַם הַגְּדִי כְּטַעַם הַצְּבִי. Rivkah: I will make them into tasty food for your father such as he loves; Rashi: for the taste of a kid is like the taste of a deer. *Mafteach: missing*

**Shabbat 30b** — שֶׁאֵין שְׁכִינָה שׁוֹרָה לֹא מִתּוֹךְ עַצְבוּת... אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ דְּבַר שִׂמְחָה שֶׁל מִצְוָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְעַתָּה קְחוּ לִי מְנַגֵּן וְהָיָה כְּנַגֵּן הַמְנַגֵּן וַתְּהִי עָלָיו יַד ה׳״. The Shechinah rests not amid sadness or idle talk but amid the joy of a mitzvah, as with Elisha's musician. Rav Tzadok's objection to Ramban: Elisha's joy was the joy of a mitzvah, not the pleasure of food. *Mafteach: found*

**Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot 8** — מְדַבֵּר בְּיִצְחָק, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת עֵשָׂו כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו. הָיָה צָד אֶת יִצְחָק הַצַּדִּיק בְּפִיו... וּמִתּוֹךְ דְּבָרִים אֵלּוּ, הָיָה צָדוֹ בְּפִיו, עַל כֵּן אֲהֵבוֹ. Esav trapped the righteous Yitzchak with his mouth, asking whether salt must be tithed; through such talk he snared him, and therefore Yitzchak loved him. *Mafteach: found*

**Shabbat 63a** (unnamed) — אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין מִקְרָא יוֹצֵא מִידֵי פְּשׁוּטוֹ. A verse does not depart from its plain sense; so the midrashic "trapping" does not displace Onkelos's "he ate of his catch". *Mafteach: missing*

**Bereshit Rabbah 63:10** — וַיֶּאֱהַב יִצְחָק אֶת עֵשָׂו כִּי צַיִד בְּפִיו, קוֹפַּרָא טָבָא לְפוּמֵיהּ, וְכַסָּא טָבָא לְפוּמֵיהּ. Good meat for his mouth and a good cup for his mouth: the midrash itself reads the verse literally. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Bereshit Rabbah 63:8; correct: Bereshit Rabbah 63:10)*

**Genesis 25:27** with **Bereshit Rabbah 63:10** — וַיְהִי עֵשָׂו אִישׁ יֹדֵעַ צַיִד אִישׁ שָׂדֶה; midrash: צָד בַּבַּיִת, צָד בַּשָּׂדֶה. בַּבַּיִת, הֵיךְ מְתַקְנִין מִלְחָא. בַּשָּׂדֶה, הֵיךְ מְתַקְנִין תִּבְנָא. Esav was a skilled hunter, a man of the field: he hunted at home, asking how salt is tithed, and in the field, asking how straw is tithed. (Rashi to 25:27 gives the same.) The index has the midrash only under the next verse; Genesis 25:27 is not indexed. *Mafteach: missing*

**Ran on the Rif, Kiddushin 16a (Rif pages; on Mishnah Kiddushin 41a)** — דמצוה בה יותר מבשלוחה דאע"ג דאשה אינה מצוה בפריה ורביה מ"מ יש לה מצוה מפני שהיא מסייעת לבעל לקיים מצותו. It is a greater mitzvah for her to accept betrothal herself: though a woman is not commanded to have children, she has a mitzvah because she helps her husband fulfil his. Rav Tzadok applies this to Yitzchak, who has a share in Esav's mitzvah of honouring a father by eating what he brings (2.21–22). *Mafteach: missing*

**Bereshit Rabbah 65:16** — אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל כָּל יָמַי הָיִיתִי מְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת אַבָּא וְלֹא שִׁמַּשְׁתִּי אוֹתוֹ אֶחָד מִמֵּאָה שֶׁשִּׁמֵּשׁ עֵשָׂו אֶת אָבִיו... אֲבָל עֵשָׂו בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהָיָה מְשַׁמֵּשׁ אֶת אָבִיו לֹא הָיָה מְשַׁמְּשׁוֹ אֶלָּא בְּבִגְדֵי מַלְכוּת. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: all my days I served my father, yet not a hundredth of how Esav served his; Esav served him only in royal garments. *Mafteach: found*

**Avodah Zarah 20a** on **Deuteronomy 7:2** — ״לֹא תְחׇנֵּם״... לֹא תִּתֵּן לָהֶם חֵן; Rashi there: שלא יאמר כמה עובד כוכבים זה נאה. "Do not show them favour": do not ascribe grace to them, such as saying "how handsome this idolater is". All the more, says Rav Tzadok, one may not praise Esav's virtue. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Bechukotai 1** (Rav Tzadok) — the same argument with the same sources: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel on Esav and Dama ben Netina (Kiddushin 31a) cannot be praise of gentiles, since "כמה נאה" is forbidden; they honour parents because reason demands it toward those who brought them into a world they prize. It adds that this is why honouring parents is called *mishpat*, a rational law, while Israel do even the *mishpatim* only as Hashem's command, and that is what brings holiness into them. *checked*

**Eruvin 13b** — נִמְנוּ וְגָמְרוּ: נוֹחַ לוֹ לְאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא נִבְרָא יוֹתֵר מִשֶּׁנִּבְרָא, עַכְשָׁיו שֶׁנִּבְרָא — יְפַשְׁפֵּשׁ בְּמַעֲשָׂיו. After two and a half years of debate it was decided: it would have been better for man not to be created; now that he has been, let him examine his deeds. *Mafteach: found*

**Kiddushin 31a** — עַד הֵיכָן כִּיבּוּד אָב וָאֵם? אָמַר לָהֶם: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ מָה עָשָׂה נׇכְרִי אֶחָד בְּאַשְׁקְלוֹן, וְדָמָא בֶּן נְתִינָה שְׁמוֹ. How far does honouring parents go? Go and see what a gentile in Ashkelon, Dama ben Netina, did: he gave up a great profit rather than wake his father. *Mafteach: found*

**Bava Kamma 38b** — אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְקַפֵּחַ שְׂכַר כׇּל בְּרִיָּה, אֲפִילּוּ שְׂכַר שִׂיחָה נָאָה. The Holy One withholds no creature's reward, even the reward for decent speech. The index also lists this saying under "Yoma" with no address; that entry should be removed. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Menorat HaMaor (Al-Nakawa), On Honouring Parents, The ways of honouring** (Mussar) — on feeding a parent, it says Esav, for all his sins, inherited this world in reward for hunting and feeding his father, and cites the same midrash on Esav's good meat for his father's mouth.
ועשו הרשע, אע"פ שהיה עושה כל עבירות שבעולם, בזכות שכיבד את אביו, והיה יוצא וצד ציד ומאכילו ומשקהו, נחל העולם הזה.

**Nazir 23b** — שֶׁבִּשְׂכַר אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁנַיִם קׇרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁהִקְרִיב בָּלָק הָרָשָׁע — זָכָה וְיָצְאָה מִמֶּנּוּ רוּת. For the forty-two offerings the wicked Balak brought, he merited that Ruth descended from him (taught there to show that one should do mitzvos even not for their own sake; also Horayot 10b, Sotah 47a). *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Nazir 10b; correct: Nazir 23b)*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Be'er Mayim Chaim, Genesis 25:26** (Chassidus) — explains Yitzchak's love for Esav from the same three sources (Onkelos, "קופרא טבא לפומיה", and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel): Yitzchak saw Esav labouring to feed his father and took it as the good in him overcoming the bad through the mitzvah of honouring a father.
והתגבר הטוב שבו על רעתו לקיים בעובדיו ומעשיו שהוא החרב, מצות ה' כיבוד אב.

**Genesis 27:3** — וְצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה וְצוּדָה לִּי (צידה) [צָיִד]. Go out to the field and hunt me game: written צידה, with a final *heh*, but read צָיִד (see Radak there: צָיִדה כְּתִיב בְּהֵ״א וּקְרֵי בְּלֹא הֵ״א). *Mafteach: found*

**The Arizal, on an added letter of the Divine Name** — cited without a place; the passage was not found in Pri Etz Chaim, Etz Chaim, Sha'ar HaKavanot, Sha'ar HaPesukim or Sha'ar Ma'amarei Razal as searched, so no wording of the Ari is quoted. Rav Tzadok states the rule several times, e.g. **Takanat HaShavin 15** (וְיָדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִיזַ״ל שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנּוֹסָף אוֹת מֵאוֹתִיּוֹת שֵׁם הֲוָיָ״ה מוֹרֶה תּוֹסֶפֶת קְדוּשָּׁה) and Takanat HaShavin 6 and 11, on the extra *vav* of בעוון. A close Chassidic parallel on this very word: **Avodat Yisrael, Toldot** reads the extra letters of וְצוּדָה ... צָיִדָה as letters of the Name (רָמַז לְאַרְבַּע אוֹתִיּוֹת הַקְּדוֹשִׁים). *Mafteach: missing*

**Bereshit Rabbah 58:7** on **Genesis 23:16** — וְלֹא יֵדַע כִּי חֶסֶר יְבֹאֶנּוּ, שֶׁחִסְּרַתּוֹ הַתּוֹרָה וָא"ו, הֲדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב: וַיִּשְׁקֹל אַבְרָהָם לְעֶפְרֹן, עֶפְרֹן כְּתִיב חָסֵר וָא"ו. "He does not know that want will come to him": the Torah took a *vav* from him; after he took the money his name is written עפרן, missing the *vav*. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Bereshit Rabbah 58:6; correct: Bereshit Rabbah 58:7)*

**Taanit 5b** — הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין מְסִיחִין בִּסְעוּדָה, שֶׁמָּא יַקְדִּים קָנֶה לְוֶשֶׁט וְיָבֹא לִידֵי סַכָּנָה. One does not talk during a meal, lest the windpipe open before the gullet and he come into danger. So, says Rav Tzadok, the blessing would not come from Yitzchak's own speech but from the Shechinah speaking through him. *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 27:7** — הָבִיאָה לִּי צַיִד וַעֲשֵׂה־לִי מַטְעַמִּים וְאֹכֵלָה וַאֲבָרֶכְכָה לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לִפְנֵי מוֹתִי. Rivkah's report of Yitzchak's words adds "before Hashem", which Yitzchak did not say (27:4). *Mafteach: found*

**Genesis 27:8–9** — וְעַתָּה בְנִי שְׁמַע בְּקֹלִי לַאֲשֶׁר אֲנִי מְצַוָּה אֹתָךְ. לֶךְ־נָא אֶל־הַצֹּאן... וְאֶעֱשֶׂה אֹתָם מַטְעַמִּים לְאָבִיךָ כַּאֲשֶׁר אָהֵב. Now, my son, obey my voice in what I command you; go now to the flock... and I will make them tasty food for your father such as he loves. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Akeidat Yitzchak 24** (Machshava) — reads the episode the same way: Yitzchak sent Esav on the hunt to give him mitzvos of honouring a father so that he would merit the blessing, and Rivkah's "obey my voice in what I command you" was meant to add to Yaakov's merit by acting at his righteous mother's command; it also notes that Rivkah added "before Hashem".
כיוונה גם היא להרבות לו זכות במה שיכוין לעשות כל מה שיעש' במצות אמו הצדקת

**Beitzah 16a** — אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל שַׁמַּאי הַזָּקֵן, כׇּל יָמָיו הָיָה אוֹכֵל לִכְבוֹד שַׁבָּת. מָצָא בְּהֵמָה נָאָה, אוֹמֵר: זוֹ לַשַּׁבָּת... אבל הלל הזקן מדה אחרת היתה לו שכל מעשיו לשם שמים שנאמר ברוך ה׳ יום יום. Shammai ate all his days in honour of Shabbat, setting aside every finer animal for Shabbat; Hillel had another way, for all his deeds were for Heaven's sake, as it says "Blessed is Hashem day by day". *Mafteach: found*
**Psalms 68:20** — בָּרוּךְ אֲדֹנָי יוֹם יוֹם יַעֲמׇס־לָנוּ. Blessed is the Lord day by day; He bears our burden. Hillel's verse, quoted in Beitzah 16a. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Tu BiShvat 2:2** (Rav Tzadok) — the same pairing of Beitzah 16a with Vayikra Rabbah 34:3: Hillel fed his body only as one feeds a guest; it adds why each took his path (Shammai, from the attribute of *pachad Yitzchak*, did not trust his own intent and so tied his eating to Shabbat; Hillel ate like Yaakov or Adam before the sin, without sensing bodily pleasure) and ties both to the Tu BiShvat dispute of their schools. *checked*

**Vayikra Rabbah 34:3** on **Proverbs 11:17** — גֹּמֵל נַפְשׁוֹ אִישׁ חָסֶד, זֶה הִלֵּל הַזָּקֵן... אָמַר לָהֶם לִגְמֹל חֶסֶד עִם הָדֵין אַכְסַנְיָא בְּגוֹ בֵּיתָא... וְהָדֵין נַפְשָׁא עֲלוּבְתָּא לָאו אַכְסַנְיָא הוּא בְּגוֹ גוּפָא, יוֹמָא דֵין הִיא הָכָא לְמָחָר לֵית הִיא הָכָא. "A kind man does good to his own soul": this is Hillel, who told his students he was going to do kindness with the guest in his house; is not this poor soul a guest in the body, here today and gone tomorrow? *Mafteach: found*

**Zohar II 204b** (Vayakhel) — הַאי רוּחָא, אִתְהֲנִי בְּהַאי יוֹמָא, מֵהֲנָאוֹתָן דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמֵעִנּוּגָא דִּלְהוֹן, וּבְגִין דָּא, בָּעֵי לְמֵיהַב לֵיהּ עִנּוּגָא, בְּמֵיכְלָא וּבְמִשְׁתְּיָא, תְּלָת זִמְנִין, בִּתְלַת סְעוּדָתִין. This spirit (the added soul) enjoys on this day the pleasures and delights of Israel; therefore one must give it delight in food and drink three times, in three meals. The Zohar's "give *it* delight" is the basis of Rav Tzadok's reading of "whoever gives delight to the Shabbat" (5.12). *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar II 189b; correct: Zohar II 204b)*

**Shabbat 118a–b** (unnamed) — כָּל הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ נַחֲלָה בְּלִי מְצָרִים (R. Yochanan, 118a); כׇּל הַמְעַנֵּג אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת נוֹתְנִין לוֹ מִשְׁאֲלוֹת לִבּוֹ (Rav, 118b). Whoever delights the Shabbat is given a boundless inheritance; is given his heart's desires. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Vayera 1:3** (Rav Tzadok) — the same precision in "המענג את השבת", built on the same Zohar (Vayakhel 204a–b, "זכאה מאן דאהני לי' ומענג לי'"): the delight belongs to the added soul, which is itself called *es haShabbos*; it adds that the *es* marks the added soul as secondary to the Shechinah it extends from. *checked*

**Zohar II 88b** (Yitro) — יַהֲבִין לֵיהּ לְבַר נָשׁ נִשְׁמְתָא אַחֲרָא, נִשְׁמְתָא עִלָּאָה, נִשְׁמְתָא דְּכָל שְׁלִימוּ בָּהּ, כְּדוּגְמָא דְּעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי. וּבְגִינֵי כַּךְ אִקְרֵי שַׁבָּת. A person is given another, higher soul, complete like the World to Come, and therefore it is called Shabbat. *Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar II 205a** (Vayakhel) — הַאי יוֹמָא, יוֹמָא דְּנִשְׁמָתִין אִיהוּ, וְלָאו יוֹמָא דְּגוּפָא, בְּגִין דְּשֻׁלְטָנוּ דִּצְרוֹרָא דְּנִשְׁמָתִין אִיהוּ. This day is a day of souls and not of the body, for it is ruled by the bundle of souls. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Ba'al Shem Tov, Bereshit 85** (Chassidus) — on the same midrash, "He blessed it with flavour", the Baal Shem Tov teaches that delighting the body on Shabbat is a mitzvah because through it the soul can rejoice more in cleaving to Hashem.
שמעתי בשם מורי טעם לענג החומר בשבת הוא מצוה, שעל ידי זה יוכל הצורה לשמוח יותר בדבקות השם יתברך

**Bereshit Rabbah 65:13** with **Genesis 3:6** — וַעֲשֵׂה לִי מַטְעַמִּים... שְׁלשָׁה דְבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בּוֹ בָּעֵץ שֶׁאָכַל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן, טוֹב לְמַאֲכָל, וְיָפֶה לָעֵינַיִם, וּמוֹסִיף חָכְמָה... וְכֵן יִצְחָק אָמַר וַעֲשֵׂה לִי מַטְעַמִּים, אָמַר לוֹ בַּתְּחִלָּה הָיִיתִי נֶהֱנֶה מִן הָרְאִיָּה, וְעַכְשָׁיו אֵינִי נֶהֱנָה אֶלָּא מִן הַטַּעַם. Three things were said of the tree Adam ate (Genesis 3:6): good to eat, pleasing to the eye, adding wisdom; so Yitzchak said: at first I enjoyed sight, now I enjoy only taste. This is the source of 5.23–24, Yitzchak's blindness. *Mafteach: missing*

**Psalms 34:9** — טַעֲמוּ וּרְאוּ כִּי־טוֹב יְהֹוָה אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר יֶחֱסֶה־בּוֹ. Taste and see that Hashem is good; happy is the man who takes refuge in Him. Rav Tzadok joins it to the midrash: holy eating has holiness in both taste and sight. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Shem MiShmuel, Toldot 10:10–12** (Chassidus) — rejects that Yitzchak wanted bodily pleasure: he sought joy so that the holy spirit would rest on him (citing Elisha's musician), and he proves from the same midrash ("at first I enjoyed sight, now only taste") that he wanted the food for joy and not for flavour; it adds that while Esav was honouring his father the holy spirit returned to Yitzchak, so he linked it to the dishes.
וכל עצמו לא נצרך לו אלא למען להיות בחדוה ובשמחה כדי שתשרה עליו רוה"ק

corrections.index_text: הקפדה שכל - תהיה - מצווה

corrections.quote: וְכֵן כָּל אֶחָד מֵהַקְּדוֹשִׁים מְחַפֵּשׂ שֶׁתִּהְיֶה אֲכִילָתוֹ סְעוּדַת מִצְוָה
corrections.note: The os speaks of making every meal a mitzvah meal; Melaveh Malkah is not mentioned.
